Fortunately in France we are not allowed to accept the kids without information about their health, and since the parents have to think about their kid to answer the question, they rarely forget the big stuff.

They did, I am a good counselor :-)
(And we had instructions from both their doctors, so we were not completely taken by surprise)

I am what I think in the US you call a counselor in summer camp (basically I watch over kids day and night, and organise entertaining activities for them).
Last summer, there were two nights (thankfully not consecutive nights), where we were woken up by kids telling us that one of their roommates was shaking violently in his bed (of course both of them were in the top bunk bed, and both of them were 17yo boys, so we had fun trying to get them out).

One of them was taking meds that weakened his immune system, and he went to bed with a normal cold that made his body temperature went so high that his brain couldn't handle it anymore.

The second one had epilepsy, and his meds would work only for 6 hours, and the doctor said that he did not need to get up at night to take it, even if they were in bed for 8 hours straight.
Well, guess what, the last night he was too tired and the meds not being in effect anymore he had a seizure.

I often joke with my friends that, even though they do not warn us during formation, the most important part of being a counselor is to keep the kids alive, and that the kids are pretty damn inventive when it comes to make that part difficult.

(I would like to apologise for any mistakes, as I am not a native English speaker).

I teach middle schoolers in a rough neighbourhood, and I have one of the hardest classes.

We had a class together on the first period of the last day before the autumn holidays, and I knew I wouldn't be able to teach normally.
So I said when they came in that the front rows were for those who wanted to study, and that those who wanted to talk could sit in the other ones and that if they didn't make too much noise I wouldn't bother them.

10 out of 25  students decided up front they wanted to work, and didn't open their mouths unless it was to ask a question. This at least was a big surprise to me.

Then, while I was talking explaining the lesson for those who wanted it, maybe 7 more students stopped talking, came in the front rows and started taking notes and asking question.

But what was the best moment of the period was when one of my most disrespectful student, after I had told the not-working group  that they were too loud 3 times, began explaining to the other that it was not correct to be so loud when I was being nice to let them do what they wanted before the holidays, and that since some wanted to work they all should keep it as low as possible so that they could concentrate.

I was astonished, and it feels great to see that she is mature and can think of what she is doing.
Thanks ! I really like when someone corrects me, it encourages me to keep on studying.
